run: a text-only comparison of the components that could write what plain Persian script leaves out - the ezafe and short vowels - before any of them goes into the app
status: registered 2026-10-03, before any component ran on either set
why: the pronunciation review (eval/runs/persian-voice-pronunciation-review-v1.json): of the 19 errors OmniVoice made on plain script, 9 are ezafe and 8 short vowels, and OmniVoice reads the diacritics it is given whether they are right or wrong. So whatever writes those marks must be accurate. This measures the candidates on text: no audio, no GPU, no OmniVoice
question: on plain script, which component places the ezafe best, and how accurately each source gives a word's vowels

hazm-crf.what: hazm 0.12.1's CRF part-of-speech tagger; a tag carrying ,EZ marks an ezafe

hazm-spacy.what: hazm 0.12.1's ParsBERT tagger through spaCy, asked for full tags (universal_tag=False keeps the ,EZ its universal tags drop)
hazm-spacy.source: roshan-research/hazm-parsbert-postagger @ eba1d2b30cc48206c0144b36d2b663652d44faf9 (655 MB; spaCy 3.6 pipeline loaded in 3.8.16 - the only weight not loaded strictly is BERT's position_ids buffer, checked 2026-10-03)

albert.what: the ezafe model of the LCA phonemizer (arXiv 2512.08006): an ALBERT student of the spaCy tagger; the label on each word's first piece, as its authors' evaluation reads it

homo-ge2pe.what: Homo-GE2PE as the app runs it: voiceclone.text.g2p.PersianG2P().phonemize (normalize_for_g2p, then GE2PE with its rules); its words are aligned to the text by consonant skeletons
homo-ge2pe.source: ~/Desktop/G2P Research/third_party/Homo-GE2PE-Persian (the weights' sha256 is recorded with the predictions)

kaamel.what: KaamelDict looked up word by word, exact spelling (diacritics dropped); a word it lists with one vowel skeleton is answered, with more or none it is not

never.what: no ezafe anywhere: what plain script tells the model

kaamel-then-homo-ge2pe.what: derived, not run: KaamelDict where it answers, Homo-GE2PE otherwise

looked_up_and_not_run.PedramR/canine-fa-diacritizer: a character diacritizer (card, 2026-07-22: 8.3% diacritic error rate on 359 sentences). Gated: access is approved automatically, but the request is made from the user's Hugging Face account and accepts the author's conditions - the user's decision
looked_up_and_not_run.AminMadani/persian-byt5-g2p: reads a word at a time, so it has no ezafe and no context for homographs; its card reports SentenceBench PER 9.64% and homograph accuracy 41.98%. Its tokenizer files need transformers 5 and its weights are 1.2 GB with 12 GB free on this disk. Not run
looked_up_and_not_run.Dadmatech/Kasreh_ezafe and AKA-Abdol/eza: older or without a card; not run

prior_evidence: arXiv 2512.08006 (Dec 2025), on its own ezafe gold from SentenceBench: spaCy tagger F1 97.67%, ALBERT 94.19%. hazm reports EZ detection F1 0.993 on its own test. Neither is this gold. Looked up 2026-10-03

environments.taggers: ~/.cache/persian-voice-cloning/frontend/.venv: Python 3.12, hazm 0.12.1, spaCy 3.8.16, spacy-transformers 1.4.0, transformers 4.53.2, torch 2.14.0 (hazm needs Python 3.12+, spacy-transformers needs transformers < 4.53.3)
environments.input: the same for every component: Arabic letter forms to Persian, tatweel dropped, spacing left alone so the words stay the gold's words (the LCA authors ran hazm's Normalizer first; that can join words, so it is not used). Taggers get punctuation as separate tokens; ALBERT gets it attached, as its authors fed it; Homo-GE2PE gets the sentence

sentencebench.gold: per word, from its annotated pronunciation: words and annotation aligned by consonant skeletons (a conjunction و merged as -o is split off; two words annotated as one are left out), and the ezafe read off the ending - a hyphenated -e/-ye, or an attached e/ye judged by the word's last letter (scripts/score_frontend_components.py ezafe_split, tested). Checked by eye on samples 2026-10-03
sentencebench.caveat: Homo-GE2PE, the ALBERT model and KaamelDict come from the group that made SentenceBench; their training data may overlap it. Before scoring, every SentenceBench sentence is looked for in HomoRich (huggingface.co/datasets/MahtaFetrat/HomoRich-G2P-Persian @ 21b189a76c15e9a899e9606c6a909d30e9dc4596, the training data named for both), and results are given per subset. The ALBERT paper says its student learned from ManaTTS text; the mana-tts subset is where that would show

review14.heard: A's 19 errors in the review, each listed with its word
review14.note: Claude wrote the readings the review does not settle, after looking 22 words up in KaamelDict (listed in the file) - which can flatter KaamelDict here

measures.ezafe: per scorable word: added (an ezafe where none belongs), missed, right; precision, recall, F1, errors per word, and sentences with no ezafe error
measures.vowels: per scorable word, the vowels of its reading in order (ezafe left out) against the gold's; for SentenceBench also the 211 located homographs. A component that gives nothing for a word has not answered it: counted in coverage, not accuracy - except Homo-GE2PE, which always answers, so a word it drops counts as wrong
measures.heard: on the 14 sentences, each of A's 19 heard errors: right or not in each component's output

decision_rules.ezafe_source: the component with the fewest ezafe errors per word on SentenceBench, subsets pooled. The 95% interval of its difference from the runner-up (paired bootstrap over sentences, 10,000 resamples, seed 20261003) decides whether they are separated. Separated: the best is step 2's ezafe source. Not separated: the one that gets more of A's 9 heard ezafe errors right, then the lighter one
decision_rules.vowels: not a choice here: the numbers set step 2's marking policy. A read the vowels of 191 of 199 words right in the review, so a source helps a word only where it beats that: if no source reaches 96% on SentenceBench, marking every word is ruled out, and step 2 marks only where needed (homographs and the words OmniVoice is known to misread), registered then
decision_rules.review14: reported, not ranked: it decides only a tie on SentenceBench. Where a component disagrees with a reading Claude wrote (not settled by the review), the word goes to the user blind - the readings, no component names - before the 14-sentence reading is final; the numbers are shown before and after

not_claimed: text only: nothing here says how OmniVoice reads the marks - that is step 2, by listening and CER. SentenceBench's ezafe gold is derived by rule from its annotation; vowel skeletons ignore consonants and where in a word a vowel sits; SentenceBench may overlap some components' training data
cost: CPU on this Mac, one component at a time; the largest, the spaCy tagger, peaked at 3.3 GB resident in its smoke test. No GPU quota
